Volcanic Eruption Disrupts Travel and Trade Across Iceland

A powerful volcanic eruption began early Tuesday morning near the Reykjanes Peninsula, sending ash clouds across southwestern Iceland and forcing authorities to close key transport routes and suspend numerous flights. The eruption, which follows weeks of heightened seismic activity, has already caused significant disruption to economic activity across the country.

Isavia Ohf, the company responsible for managing Iceland’s airports, announced closures at Keflavik International Airport, stranding thousands of passengers and halting most incoming and outgoing flights. “Safety is our highest priority. All operations are on hold until the ash disperses and it is safe to operate again,” said Jónas Þorvaldsson, a spokesperson for Isavia Ohf.

The eruption’s ash plume has also forced the temporary closure of the main highway connecting Reykjavik and the south coast, impeding the flow of goods and travelers. The Icelandic Chamber of Commerce warned that supply chains for food and fuel are under strain, with supermarkets in the capital reporting delays in deliveries. “We are coordinating with local authorities to reroute trucks where possible, but the situation remains highly uncertain,” said Sigríður Lövdal, logistics manager at the retailer Norðursjóvar.

Farmers in the affected region have begun evacuating livestock, while coastal fishing fleets remain in port until further notice. The Icelandic Association of Tourism Operators called the situation “devastating,” as hotels and tour companies receive mass cancellations from overseas visitors.

Authorities urge residents to stay indoors and monitor official updates as the eruption continues. At the time of writing, no injuries have been reported, but emergency services remain on high alert.
